questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual has information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate it, what it can do, and how to maintain it.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle accident?

options.text: Ask others about how to ride more safely.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce your risk of death or serious injury in an accident.

questions.question: What does a yellow sign with black lettering or symbols mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols warn drivers about upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: What can you do in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if the pass can be completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in a no passing zone. You also cannot pass by driving off the main road.

questions.question: What is an advantage of downshifting smoothly on a motorcycle?

options.text: It can slow the motorcycle using the engine.
You should not do it if other vehicles are around.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can slow the motorcycle using the engine.
questions.explanation: Smooth downshifting allows you to use the engine to slow down your motorcycle. If you do this, use your brake lights to tell other drivers that you are slowing down.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all dangerous for motorcycles because they reduce grip. Dry pavement is the safest surface.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can get the attention of other drivers by turning their heads.
They should try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Like any vehicle, a motorcycle has areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in these blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which fabric protects a motorcycle rider the most?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to a car?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you. Also, the car will block your escape route.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps other drivers see you any time of day. Most motorcycle accidents happen during daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day as well as at night.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of what material?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects riders from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, pebbles, and injury from crashes.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle someone tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass
Speed up to get distance between you

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to safely change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Why is it better to ride in a small group?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group
A small group can ignore traffic laws
Riders will always try to catch up to the group
It is hard to keep track of everyone

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group
questions.explanation: Small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to get separated by traffic or traffic lights, and do not force slower riders to rush to catch up.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: High boots that cover the ankle

questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, sturdy jacket and pants, high boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at traffic lights, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal road covers are slippery. Ride carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding
It does not have a chin strap

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night
Does not help you to be seen

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: For best protection, what should jackets and pants do?

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely
Be loose and flap in the wind
Only partially cover your arms and legs

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but be loose enough to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not give you the same protection as a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that helps other drivers see you and your motorcycle. Bright, reflective clothing makes it easier for others to spot you on the road.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat built for two riders to carry a passenger. The motorcycle should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: The same as a face shield

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not the rest of your face. A face shield protects your whole face and is better protection. A windshield is not enough protection on its own.

questions.question: What should boots or shoes have to protect you best?

options.text: Long laces that are not tucked in

questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they do not catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they do not catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: What helps reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals. Paint damage does not affect your safety.

questions.question: What should you wear to help other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself visible to other drivers. Choose clothes that stand out during the day and at night.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle
Not check your rearview mirrors for traffic behind you
Look for ways to squeeze through stopped traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes from behind too fast.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Prevent brakes from activating on dry roads
Warn you when brake pads need replacing

questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up during hard braking. When you apply maximum pressure to both brakes, electronic sensors detect if a wheel is about to lock. The system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep the best braking power.
